previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient, a male with HLA-B27-positive ankylosing spondylitis, hypertension, obesity, asthma, and obstructive sleep apnea, was admitted for an acute flare of left sacroiliac joint pain that severely limited his mobility and prevented him from leaving home. He reported symptoms consistent with prior flares and denied trauma, fever, or neurological changes. Due to concerns about radiation exposure, imaging was declined. He received IV hydromorphone and ketorolac for breakthrough pain and was started on a short prednisone taper based on rheumatology input, as he had previously responded well to steroids. His pain improved, and he was discharged home with a 3-day opioid supply to bridge until his outpatient prescription could be refilled. He was advised to continue all home medications, including the steroid taper, asthma inhalers, CPAP, and lisinopril. Follow-up was recommended with his primary care provider.
problems: Morbid (severe) obesity due to excess calories

Brief Hospital Course:
Mr. ___ is a ___ male with the past
medical history of HLA-B27-positive ankylosing spondylitis,
previously treated with multiple agents including sulfasalazine,
etanercept, adalimumab, infliximab and one dose of golimumab
which was self discontinued after one dose due to reported
infectious complications.  He also has a history of obesity,
GERD, chronic pain, multiple ER visits for pain, and opiate
dependence who presents to the ER with pain. 

#Acute on chronic pain syndrome - I discussed with him my
concerns for his use of narcotics and how escalating doses can
cause hyperalgesia and worsen dependence.  His exam is also
inconsistent with the pain he reports.  Based on the history and
exam, I think that it is fair to say a portion of his inability
to move is behavioral.  ___ RN also noted that when he was 
observed while he was in his room, he acted normally, watching 
Netflix without any problems.  However, when this changed to 
engaging him, he would change his behavior suddenly and 
emphysize how much pain he was in.  This situation is clearly 
complex, but I
think that perpetuating intravenous narcotics is against his
interest.  Out of respect with his prior arrangement with his
PCP, ___ will continue the home doses of his oral narcotics, 
though
the increase of frequency of PRN oxycodone to TID needs to be
confirmed with his PCP. He has requested inflammatory markers 
and
ultrasounds in the past, but since these do not affect
management, there is no utility in pursuing them here. He was 
given Toradol 15mg IV q6 and continued home lidocaine cream.  
Since he was no longer receiving IV narcotics, he elected to 
leave the hospital.  He was counseled of the dangers of doing 
so, which include worsening immobility, falls, and serious 
injury.  He understood but chose to leave against medical 
advice.
